features: HEADS UP — THE UPDATE BEHAVES DIFFERENTLY: the automatic safety backup is no longer offered when updating from a version earlier than 1.10. That backup runs BEFORE the migrations, so it can only rely on the infrastructure already present in the database about to be updated — and installations coming from 1.9.x do not have it. The confirmation screen now explicitly asks you to make a copy of the database from your hosting control panel before proceeding, exactly as has been the case for every update until today. No database migration.

The automatic pre-update backup comes back on its own for updates after 1.10.0: from then on you always start from a database that already has the infrastructure, and nothing needs to be switched back on.

Fixed a defect that made updating from 1.9.1 impossible: the "Start update" button stayed disabled and there was no way to proceed. The screen offered a safety backup that is not available on those installations, and the explicit confirmation needed to proceed without one was only shown in the case where the backup WAS available: exactly when it was needed, it was missing. No data was ever at risk — the block happened before the database was touched — but the installation stayed stuck on the confirmation screen, and so did the administrator, whom the system returns there on every visit until the update completes.

The confirmation screen now states that the update is resumable: if the page stalls or errors — which on shared hosting can happen when the migrations exceed the maximum execution time — just reload it and press again, and the update picks up where it left off instead of starting over or leaving the database half done.

Fixed: three of the twelve database changes in the update to 1.10 could not be re-run. If the update was interrupted halfway — which on shared hosting happens when the server cuts off requests that take too long — the next attempt stopped with the same hard error every time, leaving the installation with a half-migrated database and no way out from the interface. All twelve now resume without error, which is what makes the advice to press the button again actually true.

The error page of the automatic update engine now explains how to get unstuck. It used to present the standalone setup file as being for new installations only, leaving without an answer exactly the people who land there: someone with an existing installation whose update did not restart. In fact that file recognises an existing installation on its own and works in update mode — it replaces only the system files, preserves the database, documents and configuration, and returns you to the update confirmation screen when done.

Fixed: when an automatic update failed, the screen showed the version number instead of the reason — the real message survived only in the log file. You now read the actual error. And if the server runs a PHP version older than required, the same page used to stay completely blank instead of saying so: that case now shows the message too. The block on an incompatible PHP version remains in place at three levels — before the update is even prepared, on the start screen, and as a server-side guard that stops everything before anything is downloaded.

The automatic update engine is now more robust against unexpected failures: some kinds of PHP error were not being caught and would end the update silently, with no message and no rollback — leaving the impression that files download but you are never redirected. They are all handled now, with an on-screen message and automatic rollback.

The automatic update engine now looks like the guided installation: dark background, white card, logo, progress bar with percentage and a log window. It was three screens each with its own styling inherited from earlier versions; for anyone updating they are the same tool, and now they look like it.
The check for backup availability is now identical in the page and in the endpoint that starts it: the two sides can no longer disagree about when the pre-update backup is offered.

The update path from a 1.9.x is now covered by 23 tests, 17 of them new in this version: that the backup is not offered, that the endpoint refuses it, that an unreadable version in the database blocks nothing, that the backup becomes available again on its own from a 1.10 or later, that finalisation always stays reachable even without a backup, and that each of the twelve database changes survives being interrupted and resumed.
